items.optimize_reason: Regional-balance test on the champion (EBIT on assets, annual change, sector-ranked). Platform neutralization moved from SUBINDUSTRY to INDUSTRY. Subindustry groups are too thin inside EMEA (fragmented across many small countries) and APAC, so neutralizing there strips out most of the common signal and leaves idiosyncratic noise; INDUSTRY is the only granularity where every region still carries dozens to hundreds of names per group, keeping both sides of the book populated inside each region. Economics unchanged: improving operating return on assets signals real competitive gain that the market prices only gradually.

Same champion with the cross-sectional benchmark narrowed to industry while the platform neutralizes at industry level, giving a fully industry-consistent construction. Tests whether the sector-level benchmark was importing cross-industry dispersion that behaves differently across regions.

EBITDA on assets instead of EBIT. Depreciation and amortisation policy differs systematically across jurisdictions (useful-life assumptions, component accounting, IFRS versus J-GAAP treatment), and APAC heavy manufacturing carries far higher depreciation intensity than AMER services. Removing D and A makes the operating return measure far more comparable across the three GLB regions, which is exactly where the current champion loses its regional Sharpe.

Turnover-lift variant: the annual EBIT-on-assets trend plus the most recent quarterly change in the same quantity. The champion clears Sharpe and Fitness but sits at 4.33% turnover, below the 5% floor; adding the fast leg of the same economic quantity raises turnover without introducing a second unrelated signal, and the two-horizon form also confirms that the annual trend is still accelerating rather than decaying.
